# ui::Command

Header: `winui/ui/Command.hpp`.

An action together with what every control invoking it would otherwise repeat: text, an icon, a shortcut, a description and whether it may run.

[Point](../core/point.md) an [AppBarButton](../controls/app-bar-button.md#uiappbarbutton), [MenuItem](../controls/menu-flyout.md#struct-menuitem) or [SwipeItem](../layout/swipe.md#struct-swipeitem) at one, and each fills in whatever of those it has not been given itself. It takes the text and the icon, and shows the description as its tooltip. On an [AppBarButton](../controls/app-bar-button.md#uiappbarbutton) or a [MenuItem](../controls/menu-flyout.md#struct-menuitem), the shortcut fires app-wide while the control is in the window, and a menu shows it as "Ctrl+D". A [SwipeItem](../layout/swipe.md#struct-swipeitem) does not register the shortcut. A [Button](../controls/button.md#uibutton), [ToggleButton](../controls/toggle-button.md#uitogglebutton), [DropdownButton](../controls/dropdown-button.md#uidropdownbutton) or [SplitButton](../controls/split-button.md#uisplitbutton) runs the command, takes its enabled state and uses its description as the tooltip when it has none, but keeps its own text.

Every field takes a value or a binding, and every control using the command follows a bound field as it changes. With [`.enabled = has_selection`](#enabled), every button and menu item pointing at the command is enabled and disabled with `has_selection`. A control's own [`.enabled`](#enabled) still applies, so the control is enabled only while both allow it.

Write the command down once and give it to every control that offers it: `.command = save`. As with a [Property](../core/property.md), either the command or the controls may be destroyed first. A control whose command was destroyed acts as if it had none. A plain field is a value fixed at construction, as on a spec, so bind a field that should change.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::string> output{};
ui::Property<bool>        has_item{true};
ui::Command favorite{
    .text        = "Add to favorites",
    .icon        = ui::Symbol::Favorite,
    .shortcut    = ui::Ctrl + ui::Key::D,
    .description = "Mark the selected item as a favorite",
    .enabled     = has_item,
    .execute     = [&](std::string_view item) { output = "Favorited " + std::string(item); },
};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .content = {
        ui::Button{.text = "Favorite", .command = favorite, .command_parameter = "Item 1"},
        ui::Text{.text = output},
    },
});
has_item = false; // the button disables itself, and Ctrl+D does nothing
```

## text

```cpp
Binding<std::string> text {}
```

UTF-8 text, used by an app-bar button, a menu item or a swipe item that has no text of its own.

## icon

```cpp
Binding<IconSource> icon {}
```

The invoking control's icon when it has none; empty by default.

## shortcut

```cpp
Binding<KeyCombo> shortcut {}
```

The shortcut. It fires app-wide while a control offering the command is in the window, and the control shows it as its shortcut text.

## description

```cpp
Binding<std::string> description {}
```

The invoking control's tooltip, unless it has one.

## enabled

```cpp
Binding<bool> enabled {true}
```

Whether the command may run. Every control using it is disabled while this is false, on top of its own [`.enabled`](#enabled), and operator() does nothing.

## execute

```cpp
CommandHandler execute {}
```

Run by operator() with the invoking control's `.command_parameter`, while [`enabled`](#enabled).

## live_

```cpp
detail::CommandLive live_ {}
```

Internal: the current values, kept by the command itself. Never set it.

## current

```cpp
const CommandValues& current() const
```

What the fields hold right now, with each bound field's latest value.

## observe

```cpp
Subscription observe(Callback<void()> fn) const
```

Calls `fn` after any bound field changes. The returned [Subscription](../core/subscription.md) must be kept for `fn` to keep firing; a control using the command keeps one to redraw.

## operator()

```cpp
void operator()(std::string_view parameter = {}) const
```

Runs [`execute`](#execute) with `parameter` while the command is enabled; otherwise does nothing.
